lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Performance task build: informal comparative inference

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Set up the first two carefully; the rest of the build depends on them.

items.prompt: Sample A: 37, 33, 32, 52, 56. Sample B: 49, 62, 53, 47, 49. Based on the means, which sample tends to have greater values?
choices: Sample B, with a mean of 52 compared to 42.
Both samples have the same mean.
Sample B, with a mean of 42 compared to 52.
Sample A, with a mean of 42 compared to 52.

items.prompt: Sample A: 41, 39, 41, 37, 40, 37. Sample B: 46, 45, 32, 38, 42, 47. Based on the range of each sample, which sample is more consistent (less variable)?
choices: Sample A, with a range of 15 compared to 4.
Sample A, with a range of 4 compared to 15.
Both samples have the same range.
Sample B, with a range of 15 compared to 4.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A researcher wants to know about all 362 students at Lincoln Middle School. She randomly selects 74 of them to survey. What is the sample in this situation?
choices: All 362 students at Lincoln Middle School
Only the first 74 students at Lincoln Middle School on a list
The researcher's own estimate
The 74 randomly selected students at Lincoln Middle School

items.prompt: A student picks a random starting point, then surveys every 10th person from the full numbered list of shoppers at a grocery store, for a total of 40. Is this sampling method likely to produce a representative sample?
choices: No, likely not representative, because the population is too large.
Yes, likely representative — every member had a fair, known chance of being chosen.
Yes, likely representative, because the sample size is large enough.
No, likely not representative — the method favors certain members over others.

items.prompt: In a random sample of 19 shoppers at a grocery store, 1 preferred a new snack flavor. Based on this sample, about how many of the 171 shoppers at a grocery store would you expect to prefer a new snack flavor?
Five random samples of the same population produced these mean scores: 29, 45, 39, 33, 45. What is the range of these sample estimates?

A population has 4044 visitors to a science museum. Student A takes a random sample of 20. Student B takes a random sample of 41. Both use proper random selection. Whose sample is more likely to give an estimate closer to the true population value?
choices: Both are equally likely to be accurate, because both are random.
Student B's sample of 41, because larger random samples tend to produce more consistent, accurate estimates.
Neither sample is reliable unless it includes the entire population.
Student A's sample of 20, because smaller samples are easier to analyze.

items.prompt: A student surveys 94 visitors to a science museum using a simple random sample and records the results. Is it valid to generalize this result to all 3196 visitors to a science museum?
choices: Yes, because the sample was selected randomly, so it is likely representative of the population.
No, because samples can never be generalized to a population.
Yes, because the sample size is large enough regardless of how it was chosen.
No, because the sample was not randomly selected, so it may not represent the population.

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Carry the build to a result and state the check that would catch an error in it.

items.prompt: A sample of 7 values is: 52, 87, 86, 43, 70, 84, 79. What is the median of this data set?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: A data set has 6 values: 32, 32, 24, 30, 29, 23. What is the new mean if an outlier of 73 is added to the data set, making 7 values in all?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
